title: A review of the Effects of the Physical Components of the Interior Space of Architecture on Emotions with an Emphasis on Neuroarchitecture

findings.consequent: Activity in anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), pleasure, arousal, aesthetic preference
findings.quote: The results of this study have shown a strong effect of curved geometries on activity in the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC). Theta band activity in ACC... indicates that the pleasure rating was higher in these conditions than in interior spaces. Participants without design expertise tend to prefer curved spaces... architects prefer orthogonal spaces, while non-architects preferred curved spaces.

findings.antecedent: Furnished spaces (arrangement and type of furniture)
findings.consequent: Arousal, heart rate, theta power in the brain, positive emotions
findings.quote: Higher arousal ranks in furnished spaces and increased heart rate and greater theta power in the space. The perception of pleasant and modern interior spaces activates visual-spatial processing areas in the frontal-occipital network and indicates the involvement of motor and cognitive processes during the evaluation of spaces and will stimulate positive emotions.

findings.consequent: Tension, fatigue, autonomic nervous system (ANS) response, respiratory system, visual system, emotions
findings.quote: The results showed that there was less tension and fatigue in the wooden rooms than in the non-wooden rooms... wooden rooms have a valuable role in physiological settings and ease of performance... the presence of materials such as wood... changes his emotions with the ANS response and reduces fatigue.

findings.consequent: Sense of pleasure, perception of beauty, decision to leave, activation of anterior medial cortex (aMCC) associated with fear processing
findings.quote: rooms with low height and indoors induce a feeling of disgust and decision to leave in people, while a room with higher height and outdoors evokes a feeling of pleasure. Short and confined ceilings induce the activation of the anterior medial cortex (aMCC)... aMCC (a region that receives direct input from the amygdala and is involved in fear processing).

findings.antecedent: Doors with medium and large widths (architectural details)
findings.quote: Moreover, the final result of placement in front of doors with medium and large widths causes arousal.

findings.antecedent: VR-simulated office spaces with access to nature (biophilic interventions)
findings.quote: biophilic interventions can help reduce stress and improve creativity. Moreover, these effects are related to both types of biophilic elements and may differ based on the type of workspace (outdoor vs. indoor). This research shows that VR-simulated office spaces with access to nature reduce stress, while indoors are more arousal.
